q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a vacuum flask?
title: Vacuum flask carbon footprint per flask
short: Weigh the inner and outer stainless steel walls, the cap and the seal per flask and multiply by supplier figures. Add drawing, welding, vacuum brazing, polishing and coating energy, then divide the plant's energy by flasks made.

ul: Stainless steel for the inner and outer walls.
Drawing and welding the two walls.
Evacuating and sealing in a vacuum furnace.

p: Report per flask by capacity and weight. The vacuum furnace is often a large energy user.

example.title: Worked example: plant energy per flask (one month)
lines: Plant total: 42,600 / 40,000 = 1.065 kg CO2 per flask
Add stainless steel and cap for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
